Based on the provided context, which appears to be excerpts from the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) in South Africa, "direct marketing" is defined as follows:

"...to approach a data subject, either in person or by mail or electronic communication, for the direct or indirect purpose of—
(a) promoting or offering to supply, in the ordinary course of business, any goods or services to the data subject; or
(b) requesting the data subject to make a donation of any kind for any reason..."

In simpler terms, direct marketing refers to approaching individuals (data subjects) with offers to sell them products or services, or asking for donations. This can be done in person, by mail, or through electronic communication such as emails, text messages, etc.

It's worth noting that the Act also provides specific requirements for direct marketing, including the need for clear identification of the sender and contact details for recipients who wish to opt-out or request further information.
